claude.sample_unit: LLM responses (48 scenarios x 5 models x 2 conditions)
models_evaluated: Five large language models (names not reported in text)

links.outcome: Clinical appropriateness and concordance of LLM answers with vs without structured framework prompt
links.effect: Clinical Appropriateness Score rose 75.0 to 80.6; strict concordance 24.6% to 37.9%, concentrated in responses with prohibited proprietary names (14.2% to 40.8%); non-acceptable 7.1% to 3.3% not significant.
links.quote: Structured prompting improved recommendation quality, but did not produce a detectable concordance gain among terminology-compliant responses.

links.outcome: Concordance of LLM endodontic recommendations with expert-preferred file group
links.effect: Strict concordance with the expert-preferred group was 24.6% under label-only, rising to 37.9% with framework; 5.2% of responses overall non-acceptable.
links.quote: Strict concordance with the expert-preferred group rose from 24.6% to 37.9%, but this gain was concentrated among responses containing prohibited proprietary names, which increased from 14.2% to 40.8%.

unlisted_practices: Providing a structured domain-specific framework in the prompt to constrain LLM recommendations for endodontic instrumentation
